column3: The participle being dead is rendered as a finite clause.
The age of this world is rendered as “the ways of this world.”
The desires of the flesh and thoughts are expanded as cravings and indulging desires and thoughts.
“God,” “with Christ,” and “with Him” make the subjects and accompaniment explicit.
Walking in the prepared works is rendered as having them “as our way of life.”
“Remember” is repeated from the preceding context.
Becoming near is rendered passively as “have been brought near.”
“In His flesh” is placed in BSB’s next verse.
The phrase “in His flesh” is in verse 14 in the Greek; “He did this” supplies a clause.
Every building is rendered as “the whole building.”
